title: Add records importer with manifest and self-check
summary: Add a new athena-core module, which already depends on both athena-git and athena-data. It copies records/ at C0 to the athena/records branch in one commit with import-manifest.json, then re-reads the commit and fails on any path, blob, hash or count mismatch. It refuses a second import. The audience is the maintainer and the later cutover job (job 7). Nothing calls it from the pipeline or runs it against main.

defaults_applied.how: Reuses RecordsWriter, ImportManifest and the existing sha2 crate; builds no new tooling.
Scratch-repository tests; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria check the failing and passing import outcomes, not that types exist.
One module plus the lib.rs registration and a doc note.
Behavior criteria name the cargo commands the verifier can run.
An empty records/ is an error, and the self-check compares counts.
Module docs explain the import and the self-check for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The importer lives in athena-core, because athena-git and athena-data do not depend on each other and athena-core depends on both. I read the Cargo.toml files to establish this.

The entry point takes a Git handle and a C0 commit id. It returns the new commit id or a typed error. It uses RecordsWriter::append with one Change::put per file plus import-manifest.json, in a single commit.

import-manifest.json sits at the root of the records branch. The paths in the manifest are the source paths as they appear at C0, under records/. The imported files go at those same paths, as the request says.
Importing twice is refused by checking that the branch already has a tip before writing. The writer's same-bytes no-op is not enough, because it would silently pass.
Binary files are copied as bytes. The scratch repository tests use the existing athena-git testutil helper. The id and timestamp for the manifest come from RecordId::generate and the current time.
An empty records/ at C0 is an error, because ImportManifest::validate rejects an empty paths list and an empty import must not count as success.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-core records_import`. A test on a scratch repository with several nested files under records/ imports them. The importer's self-check passes. The new commit on athena/records has every records/ file at the same path with the same blob id. It also holds import-manifest.json.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core records_import`. The manifest parses as HistoryRecord::ImportManifest and validates. It lists each source path with its blob id at C0 and the SHA-256 of its contents. The entry count equals the file count at C0.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core records_import`. The self-check fails with a distinct error for each of three cases: a file missing from the imported commit, a file whose bytes changed, and an extra file not in C0. A count mismatch is also covered. A passing import is not what proves these.
Run `cargo test -p athena-core records_import`. A second import into a repository that already has the records branch is refused, and the branch tip is unchanged.

No existing caller, CLI command, job pipeline step or workflow invokes the importer, and nothing is run against this repository's main. The diff touches no athena.toml, defaults.toml or .github/workflows file. The importer module docs say the importer is not wired in.
Run `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. All pass, and the importer reuses RecordsWriter and ImportManifest rather than reimplementing them.
The design doc's job-2 status text and the CHANGELOG say the importer exists and is not yet run against main, and a reader can see where the code lives.

out_of_scope: Running the importer against this repository's main or on the real records/ directory
Wiring the importer into the job pipeline, the CLI or CI
Cutover (job 7), host rules, and the other record writers
departures: The cost and wall-time percentiles are slightly above the reference. The change needs a new module with several failure-path tests on a scratch git repository, and the design leaves the module's home crate open.
